subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub define a public skill-compatibility and task-context recommendation contract, or keep skill selection and load policy entirely in OpenClaw and operator guidance?
rationale: The missing behavior crosses registry schema, recommendation/privacy inputs, and runtime instruction semantics, so the permanent ownership boundary cannot be inferred safely from current code.

options.title: Define a narrow registry contract
options.body: Specify declarative skill compatibility metadata and privacy-preserving recommendation inputs while leaving runtime enforcement to OpenClaw.

options.title: Keep registry metadata minimal
options.body: Document pruning, layering, and pinning while leaving task selection and conflict resolution entirely to OpenClaw or operators.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Retain this as low-priority research until stronger usage data identifies stable metadata and loading semantics.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow registry contract
recommendation.body: Specify declarative skill compatibility metadata and privacy-preserving recommendation inputs while leaving runtime enforcement to OpenClaw.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the largest set of adjacent ClawHub skill metadata, detail, documentation, and CLI surfaces.
